name: PagerDuty
description: Protects against destructive PagerDuty CLI/API operations like deleting \ services and schedules (which can break incident routing).

destructive_patterns.name: pd-service-delete
destructive_patterns.description: pd service delete removes a PagerDuty service, which can break incident routing.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a PagerDuty service removes all incident routing, integrations, and \ escalation policies attached to it. Incidents will no longer be created for \ this service, potentially causing outages to go unnoticed.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - pd service list: Verify the service before deletion \ - Disable the service temporarily instead of deleting \ - Export service configuration via API before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: pd-schedule-delete
destructive_patterns.description: pd schedule delete removes a PagerDuty schedule.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a schedule removes all on-call rotations and overrides. Escalation \ policies using this schedule will have gaps in coverage, potentially leaving \ incidents unassigned.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - pd schedule get <id>: Review schedule details first \ - Update the schedule rather than deleting \ - Check which escalation policies reference this schedule

destructive_patterns.name: pd-escalation-policy-delete
destructive_patterns.description: pd escalation-policy delete removes a PagerDuty escalation policy.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an escalation policy breaks incident routing for all services using \ it. Incidents may not be escalated properly, leading to delayed response \ times.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review which services use this escalation policy \ - Update the policy rather than deleting \ - Assign services to a different policy before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: pd-user-delete
destructive_patterns.description: pd user delete removes a PagerDuty user.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a user removes them from all schedules and escalation policies. \ On-call coverage may have gaps, and incident history associated with this \ user may be affected.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Deactivate the user instead of deleting \ - Reassign their schedule shifts first \ - Transfer incident ownership before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: pd-team-delete
destructive_patterns.description: pd team delete removes a PagerDuty team.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a team removes the organizational grouping and may affect access \ controls, service ownership, and escalation policies.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - pd team list: Verify the team before deletion \ - Reassign team members and services first \ - Merge teams rather than delete

destructive_patterns.name: pagerduty-api-delete-service
destructive_patterns.description: PagerDuty API DELETE /services/{id} deletes a PagerDuty service.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Direct API deletion of a service removes all incident routing immediately. \ There is no confirmation prompt when using curl directly.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET the service first to verify the ID \ - Use the pd CLI for better feedback \ - Export service configuration before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: pagerduty-api-delete-schedule
destructive_patterns.description: PagerDuty API DELETE /schedules/{id} deletes a PagerDuty schedule.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
API deletion of a schedule removes on-call rotations immediately. Escalation \ policies referencing this schedule will have coverage gaps.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET the schedule first to verify the ID \ - Use the pd CLI for better feedback \ - Check dependent escalation policies before deletion
